desc: Hired exactly 365 days before leave start meets the 12-month service test for CFRA and FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; 29 CFR 825.104, 825.110, 825.111; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla

desc: Hired 364 days before leave start is one day short of 12 months, so neither CFRA nor FMLA applies.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; 29 CFR 825.104, 825.110, 825.111; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla

desc: Exactly 1,250 hours in the prior 12 months meets the hours test.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; 29 CFR 825.110(a)(2)

desc: 1,249 hours in the prior 12 months fails the hours test for both CFRA and FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; 29 CFR 825.110(a)(2)

desc: An employer with 5 employees is covered by CFRA and PDL but not FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; Gov. Code 12945(a)(1); 2 CCR 11035(f), 11042(a) (4 months = 17 1/3 weeks); 2 CCR 11093(c) (PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently; FMLA runs with PDL); 29 CFR 825.104(a)

desc: An employer with 4 employees is not covered by CFRA, PDL or bereavement leave, so there is no job-protected leave.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; Gov. Code 12945(a)(1); 2 CCR 11035(f), 11042(a) (4 months = 17 1/3 weeks); 2 CCR 11093(c) (PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently; FMLA runs with PDL); Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave)

desc: An employer with 49 employees is not FMLA-covered but the employee still gets CFRA.
source: 29 CFR 825.104(a); Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/

desc: An employer with 50 employees within 75 miles is FMLA-covered and the employee is FMLA-eligible.
With 50+ employees but fewer than 50 within 75 miles, the employer is FMLA-covered but the employee is not FMLA-eligible; CFRA has no 75-mile rule.
source: 29 CFR 825.104(a) (employer coverage), 825.110(a)(3), 825.111 (75-mile is an employee eligibility test); Gov. Code 12945.2 (no worksite test)

desc: Hired 2027-03-01 with leave starting 2028-02-29 is 365 days but not yet 12 calendar months, so CFRA does not apply yet.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; 29 CFR 825.110(b)

desc: Employee who already used 4 weeks of CFRA in the rolling 12 months has 8 weeks left.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a) (12 workweeks in 12-month period); 2 CCR 11090(b)

desc: Employee who used all 12 weeks of CFRA and FMLA has no job-protected leave left.
Hired long ago with 2,080 hours is eligible for both laws with a full 12 weeks remaining.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; 29 CFR 825.104, 825.110, 825.111; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla

desc: 10 weeks of PDL then 12 weeks of CFRA bonding: PDL ends day 70, bonding runs 12 weeks after that, all job-protected.
source: Gov. Code 12945(a)(1); 2 CCR 11035(f), 11042(a) (4 months = 17 1/3 weeks); 2 CCR 11093(c) (PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently; FMLA runs with PDL); Unemp. Ins. Code 2627 (7-day waiting period); https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/About_DI/; Unemp. Ins. Code 3301 (8 weeks in 12 months, no waiting period since 2018), 3302; https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/paid-family-leave/

desc: Requesting 20 weeks of pregnancy disability caps PDL at 17.33 weeks (121 days) and bonding starts after that.
source: Gov. Code 12945(a)(1); 2 CCR 11035(f), 11042(a) (4 months = 17 1/3 weeks); 2 CCR 11093(c) (PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently; FMLA runs with PDL)

desc: Exactly 17.33 weeks of PDL ends 121 days after start.
source: Gov. Code 12945(a)(1); 2 CCR 11035(f), 11042(a) (4 months = 17 1/3 weeks); 2 CCR 11093(c) (PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently; FMLA runs with PDL)

desc: A 6-month employee at a 20-person employer gets PDL (no service requirement) but bonding is not CFRA-protected.
source: Gov. Code 12945(a)(1); 2 CCR 11035(f), 11042(a) (4 months = 17 1/3 weeks); 2 CCR 11093(c) (PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently; FMLA runs with PDL); Gov. Code 12945.2(a)

desc: PDL has no hours requirement: 1,000 hours at a 100-person employer gets PDL but no CFRA or FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945(a)(1); 2 CCR 11035(f), 11042(a) (4 months = 17 1/3 weeks); 2 CCR 11093(c) (PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently; FMLA runs with PDL); 2 CCR 11035 (no length-of-service requirement)

desc: At a 4-employee employer there is no PDL or CFRA, but SDI and PFL still pay.
source: Gov. Code 12945(a)(1); 2 CCR 11035(f), 11042(a) (4 months = 17 1/3 weeks); 2 CCR 11093(c) (PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently; FMLA runs with PDL); Unemp. Ins. Code 2627 (7-day waiting period); https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/About_DI/; Unemp. Ins. Code 3301 (8 weeks in 12 months, no waiting period since 2018), 3302; https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/paid-family-leave/

desc: PDL does not use up CFRA, but an employee who used 6 CFRA weeks earlier this year only has 6 protected bonding weeks.
source: Gov. Code 12945(a)(1); 2 CCR 11035(f), 11042(a) (4 months = 17 1/3 weeks); 2 CCR 11093(c) (PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently; FMLA runs with PDL); Gov. Code 12945.2(a)

desc: Pregnancy leave requested on a Thursday before Thanksgiving: notice skips the two company holidays and cert is 15 calendar days out.
source: 29 CFR 825.300(b) (eligibility notice within 5 business days), 825.300(d) (designation within 5 business days), 825.305(b) (at least 15 calendar days for certification); 2 CCR 11091(b)

desc: SDI for pregnancy disability starts paying on day 8 after a 7-day waiting period.
source: Unemp. Ins. Code 2627 (7-day waiting period); https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/About_DI/

desc: Six weeks of own serious health condition leave is fully CFRA and FMLA protected and paid by SDI from day 8, not PFL.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; Unemp. Ins. Code 2627 (7-day waiting period); https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/About_DI/

desc: Requesting 16 weeks exceeds the 12-week CFRA entitlement, so protection ends at 12 weeks.
With 9 CFRA weeks already used, a 6-week request is protected for only 3 weeks.
At a 10-person employer, own health leave is CFRA only.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a), (b)(2), (b)(4); 2 CCR 11087(e), 11088(b); https://calcivilrights.ca.gov/family-medical-pregnancy-leave/; 29 CFR 825.104

desc: Caring for a parent is covered by CFRA, FMLA and PFL; SDI does not pay.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; 29 CFR 825.102 (spouse, parent, son or daughter), 825.122; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28f-fmla-qualifying-reasons; Unemp. Ins. Code 3301 (8 weeks in 12 months, no waiting period since 2018), 3302; https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/paid-family-leave/

desc: Caring for a parent-in-law is covered by CFRA and PFL but not FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; 29 CFR 825.102 (spouse, parent, son or daughter), 825.122; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28f-fmla-qualifying-reasons; Unemp. Ins. Code 3302 (PFL family members)

desc: Caring for a grandparent is covered by CFRA and PFL but not FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; 29 CFR 825.102 (spouse, parent, son or daughter), 825.122; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28f-fmla-qualifying-reasons; Unemp. Ins. Code 3302 (PFL family members)

desc: Caring for a sibling is covered by CFRA and PFL but not FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; 29 CFR 825.102 (spouse, parent, son or daughter), 825.122; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28f-fmla-qualifying-reasons; Unemp. Ins. Code 3302 (PFL family members)

desc: Caring for a grandchild is covered by CFRA and PFL but not FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; 29 CFR 825.102 (spouse, parent, son or daughter), 825.122; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28f-fmla-qualifying-reasons; Unemp. Ins. Code 3302 (PFL family members)

desc: Caring for a registered domestic partner is covered by CFRA and PFL but not FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; 29 CFR 825.102 (spouse, parent, son or daughter), 825.122; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28f-fmla-qualifying-reasons; Unemp. Ins. Code 3302 (PFL family members)

desc: Caring for a spouse is covered by CFRA, FMLA and PFL.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; 29 CFR 825.102 (spouse, parent, son or daughter), 825.122; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28f-fmla-qualifying-reasons

desc: Caring for a child is covered by CFRA, FMLA and PFL.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; 29 CFR 825.102 (spouse, parent, son or daughter), 825.122; https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28f-fmla-qualifying-reasons

desc: Caring for a designated person in 2026 is CFRA-protected but PFL does not pay until July 1, 2028, and FMLA does not apply.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; SB 590 (2025), Unemp. Ins. Code 3302 designated person effective July 1, 2028; https://www.californiaworkplacelawblog.com/2025/10/articles/disability-and-leave/senate-bill-590-californias-state-paid-family-leave-extended-to-cover-leave-for-designated-persons/

desc: Caring for a designated person with leave starting after July 1, 2028 is paid by PFL.
source: SB 590 (2025), Unemp. Ins. Code 3302 designated person effective July 1, 2028; https://www.californiaworkplacelawblog.com/2025/10/articles/disability-and-leave/senate-bill-590-californias-state-paid-family-leave-extended-to-cover-leave-for-designated-persons/
ambiguous: Depends on whether the engine models the July 1, 2028 effective date; EDD may also decide eligibility by claim effective date, not leave start.

desc: Designated-person leave starting December 2027 still gets no PFL.
source: SB 590 (2025), Unemp. Ins. Code 3302 designated person effective July 1, 2028; https://www.californiaworkplacelawblog.com/2025/10/articles/disability-and-leave/senate-bill-590-californias-state-paid-family-leave-extended-to-cover-leave-for-designated-persons/

desc: A 10-week family care leave gets at most 8 weeks of PFL.
source: Unemp. Ins. Code 3301 (8 weeks in 12 months, no waiting period since 2018), 3302; https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/paid-family-leave/

desc: Parent-in-law care at an 8-person employer is CFRA-protected with no FMLA.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b) (child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, sibling, spouse, domestic partner, designated person); 2 CCR 11087; 29 CFR 825.104

desc: 12 weeks of baby bonding is CFRA and FMLA protected with 8 weeks of PFL starting at leave start.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(b)(4)(A); 29 CFR 825.120; Unemp. Ins. Code 3301 (8 weeks in 12 months, no waiting period since 2018), 3302; https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/paid-family-leave/

desc: Bonding at a 10-person employer is CFRA-protected only.
An employee with 1,000 hours has no job-protected bonding leave but PFL still pays.
source: Gov. Code 12945.2(a); Unemp. Ins. Code 3301 (8 weeks in 12 months, no waiting period since 2018), 3302; https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/paid-family-leave/

desc: A 5-week bonding leave gets 5 weeks of PFL.
source: Unemp. Ins. Code 3301 (8 weeks in 12 months, no waiting period since 2018), 3302; https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/paid-family-leave/

desc: Employee hired exactly 30 days before leave start is eligible for bereavement leave.
source: Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave)
ambiguous: 'Employed for at least 30 days prior to commencement' read as start minus hire >= 30 calendar days.

desc: Employee hired 29 days before leave start is not yet eligible for bereavement leave.
source: Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave)

desc: Five bereavement days starting Monday run Monday to Friday.
source: Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave)

desc: Seven bereavement days exceeds the 5 required days, so protection ends after the 5th workday.
source: Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave)
ambiguous: Whether plan.end should cover all 7 requested days is a product choice, so it is not asserted.

desc: Bereavement starting on a Saturday begins counting on Monday.
source: Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave)

desc: Five bereavement days from the Wednesday before Thanksgiving skip Thursday and Friday company holidays.
source: Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave)

desc: A 4-employee employer is not required to give bereavement leave.
source: Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave)

desc: Bereavement requested the Wednesday before Christmas: confirm skips Dec 25 and the weekend.
source: Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave); product task convention

desc: Death of a parent-in-law qualifies for bereavement leave.
source: Gov. Code 12945.7 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, 5 days, documentation within 30 days of first day of leave) (family member per 12945.2: includes parent-in-law)

desc: Five reproductive loss days for an eligible employee are fully protected.
source: Gov. Code 12945.6 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, up to 5 days per event, 20 days max in 12 months)

desc: With 15 days used, 5 more days reaches exactly the 20-day cap and is fully protected.
source: Gov. Code 12945.6 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, up to 5 days per event, 20 days max in 12 months)

desc: With 17 days used, only 3 of 5 requested days are protected under the 20-day cap.
source: Gov. Code 12945.6 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, up to 5 days per event, 20 days max in 12 months)

desc: With 20 days used in the last 12 months, no reproductive loss days remain protected.
source: Gov. Code 12945.6 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, up to 5 days per event, 20 days max in 12 months)

desc: Seven reproductive loss days exceeds the 5-day per-event limit.
source: Gov. Code 12945.6 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, up to 5 days per event, 20 days max in 12 months)

desc: Employee hired 29 days before start is not yet eligible for reproductive loss leave.
source: Gov. Code 12945.6 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, up to 5 days per event, 20 days max in 12 months)

desc: Repro loss requested Thursday July 2, 2026: confirm skips the July 3 company holiday and weekend.
source: Gov. Code 12945.6 (5+ employees, employed 30 days, up to 5 days per event, 20 days max in 12 months); product task convention

desc: On the 89th day of employment the employee cannot yet use sick leave.
source: Labor Code 246(c) (use beginning 90th day of employment), 246(d) (employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, as amended by SB 616); https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm
ambiguous: Hire date counted as day 1, so the 90th day is hire + 89 days. An implementation that requires 90 elapsed days would be one day late.

desc: On the 90th day of employment (hire + 89 days) the employee may use accrued sick leave.
source: Labor Code 246(c) (use beginning 90th day of employment), 246(d) (employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, as amended by SB 616); https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm

desc: With 60 hours banked, only 40 hours are usable this year, so a 48-hour request is over the limit.
source: Labor Code 246(c) (use beginning 90th day of employment), 246(d) (employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, as amended by SB 616); https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm

desc: 30 hours banked and 16 used this year leaves 24 usable hours; a 24-hour request over Thanksgiving spans 3 business days.
source: Labor Code 246(c) (use beginning 90th day of employment), 246(d) (employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, as amended by SB 616); https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm

desc: An employee who already used 40 hours this year has no usable sick leave left.
source: Labor Code 246(c) (use beginning 90th day of employment), 246(d) (employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, as amended by SB 616); https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm
ambiguous: The law lets an employer cap use at 40 hours or 5 days; if 5 days is more hours for this employee, some use could still be allowed.

desc: Paid sick leave applies to every employer size, including 3 employees.
source: Labor Code 246(c) (use beginning 90th day of employment), 246(d) (employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, as amended by SB 616); https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm

desc: Sick leave requested Thursday July 2, 2026 must be recorded within 3 business days, skipping July 3.
source: Labor Code 247.5, 246(i) (recordkeeping); product task convention

desc: A 16-hour request with only 10 hours banked exceeds what is available.
source: Labor Code 246(c) (use beginning 90th day of employment), 246(d) (employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, as amended by SB 616); https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm

desc: A $15,000 high quarter is in the 90% band.
source: EDD Paid Family Leave benefit amounts (2026 table: 90% to $16,279.90, flat $1,127 to $20,931.30, then 70%, max $1,765): https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/Calculating_PFL_Benefit_Payment_Amounts

desc: At the top of the 90% band ($16,279.90 high quarter) the benefit is 90% of weekly wages.
source: EDD Paid Family Leave benefit amounts (2026 table: 90% to $16,279.90, flat $1,127 to $20,931.30, then 70%, max $1,765): https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/Calculating_PFL_Benefit_Payment_Amounts

desc: One cent above the 90% band, the 2026 table pays the flat middle amount (about $1,127).
source: EDD Paid Family Leave benefit amounts (2026 table: 90% to $16,279.90, flat $1,127 to $20,931.30, then 70%, max $1,765): https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/Calculating_PFL_Benefit_Payment_Amounts

desc: A $40,000 high quarter is capped at the $1,765 2026 maximum.
source: Unemp. Ins. Code 2655 (as amended by SB 951); EDD 2026 max WBA $1,765 https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/about_edd/quick-stats/max-weekly-benefit-amount-2026.pdf; DE 2588 https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/pdf_pub_ctr/de2588.pdf

desc: A $32,760 high quarter pays $1,764.00, just under the cap.
source: Unemp. Ins. Code 2655 (as amended by SB 951); EDD 2026 max WBA $1,765 https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/about_edd/quick-stats/max-weekly-benefit-amount-2026.pdf; DE 2588 https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/pdf_pub_ctr/de2588.pdf

desc: A $32,779 high quarter computes to $1,765.03 and is capped at $1,765.
source: Unemp. Ins. Code 2655 (as amended by SB 951); EDD 2026 max WBA $1,765 https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/about_edd/quick-stats/max-weekly-benefit-amount-2026.pdf; DE 2588 https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/pdf_pub_ctr/de2588.pdf

desc: A $500 high quarter computes below $50 and is raised to the $50 minimum.
source: Unemp. Ins. Code 2655 (as amended by SB 951); EDD 2026 max WBA $1,765 https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/about_edd/quick-stats/max-weekly-benefit-amount-2026.pdf; DE 2588 https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/pdf_pub_ctr/de2588.pdf

desc: Own-health leave requested Thursday Nov 19, 2026: notice in 5 business days skips Thanksgiving holidays; cert 15 calendar days.
source: 29 CFR 825.300(b) (eligibility notice within 5 business days), 825.300(d) (designation within 5 business days), 825.305(b) (at least 15 calendar days for certification); 2 CCR 11091(b)

desc: Bonding requested Monday Dec 21, 2026: designate notice in 5 business days skips Christmas.
source: 29 CFR 825.300(b) (eligibility notice within 5 business days), 825.300(d) (designation within 5 business days), 825.305(b) (at least 15 calendar days for certification); 2 CCR 11091(b)

desc: Family care requested Thursday July 2, 2026: notice skips the July 3 observed holiday.
source: 29 CFR 825.300(b) (eligibility notice within 5 business days), 825.300(d) (designation within 5 business days), 825.305(b) (at least 15 calendar days for certification); 2 CCR 11091(b)

desc: A need learned on Saturday June 6, 2026 starts counting business days on Monday.
source: 29 CFR 825.300(b) (eligibility notice within 5 business days), 825.300(d) (designation within 5 business days), 825.305(b) (at least 15 calendar days for certification); 2 CCR 11091(b)

desc: Own-health leave requested Wednesday Dec 30, 2026: notice skips Jan 1, 2027.
source: 29 CFR 825.300(b) (eligibility notice within 5 business days), 825.300(d) (designation within 5 business days), 825.305(b) (at least 15 calendar days for certification); 2 CCR 11091(b)

desc: From $20,931.31 high quarter, the 2026 table pays 70% of weekly wages.
source: EDD Paid Family Leave benefit amounts (2026 table: 90% to $16,279.90, flat $1,127 to $20,931.30, then 70%, max $1,765): https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/Calculating_PFL_Benefit_Payment_Amounts

desc: A 10-hour-shift employee who used 40 hours this year still has 10 usable hours, because the limit is 5 days (50 hours).
source: Lab. Code § 246(i)(1) and (d), as amended by SB 616 (2023): employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, whichever is more; accrual cap 80 hours or 10 days. https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm

desc: An 8-hour-shift employee who used 40 hours this year has none left, since 5 days is also 40 hours.
source: Lab. Code § 246(i)(1) and (d), as amended by SB 616 (2023): employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, whichever is more; accrual cap 80 hours or 10 days. https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm

desc: 20 sick hours for a 10-hour-shift employee is 2 workdays, Monday and Tuesday.
source: Lab. Code § 246(i)(1) and (d), as amended by SB 616 (2023): employer may limit use to 40 hours or 5 days per year, whichever is more; accrual cap 80 hours or 10 days. https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/Paid_Sick_Leave.htm

desc: A 20-hour-a-week employee unable to work for 20 weeks still gets PDL for 17 1/3 calendar weeks when the leave is continuous.
source: 2 CCR § 11042(a): four months means the time the employee would normally work in 17 1/3 weeks; part-time employees are prorated. https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/2-CCR-11042

desc: A 40-hour-a-week employee has about 693 hours of pregnancy leave.
source: 2 CCR § 11042(a): four months means the time the employee would normally work in 17 1/3 weeks; part-time employees are prorated. https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/2-CCR-11042
